text: Agile methodology is a way of working that helps teams build products step by step. Instead of planning everything at the start, the work is broken into small time periods called sprints, usually lasting one to four weeks. Each morning, the team has a short meeting called a standup, where everyone shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any problems they face. Before starting a sprint, the team chooses tasks from a list called the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from a user's perspective, such as "As a customer, I want to track my order." This iterative approach allows for regular feedback and quick changes, making the final product more useful.
